justification: Flood JRC/WOfS blanks persisted because the BINDING limits are the INNER timeouts, not the outer wrappers changed before. JRC reads a remote GeoTIFF via GDAL vsicurl bounded by GDAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT=12s (raised to 30, with the outer fut.result 35->60); WOfS downloads a WCS GeoTIFF bounded by requests timeout=20s (raised to 30, with _WOFS_HARD_TIMEOUT 35->60); the brief's flood collection budget raised 50->70s so the now-longer concurrent sub-queries (max ~60s) are not cut off. Since JRC/WOfS return 0 for a genuine no-water reading and null only on a FAILED read, the frontend now renders 'Couldn't retrieve' for a null JRC/WOfS/EPI-flood instead of an ambiguous '—'. Also labelled the nearby-DA radius explicitly as 500 m. Companion change (separate repo): the Trigger.dev task maxDuration 120->300 so the longer brief finishes before the stream is cut.

pre_impl.existing_data: JRC _query_jrc_surface_water samples via /vsicurl with GDAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT=12 and an outer 35s; WOfS _query_dea_wofs downloads a WCS GeoTIFF with requests timeout=20 and an outer 35s; both return null on failure and a real float (incl 0.0) on success. The brief collected flood at a hardcoded 50s.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Earlier I raised the outer wrappers (25->35), but the inner GDAL/requests timeouts fired first, so the reads still failed fast and returned null (rendered blank).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Bumped existing inner+outer timeout constants keeping inner < outer; reused the existing null-on-failure contract for the honest 'couldn't retrieve' render.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Slow JRC GCS / DEA WCS reads now get more time; a still-failing read stays null and shows 'Couldn't retrieve' rather than a misleading dash or a false 0.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend timeouts + a frontend honest-null render + a label. tsc passes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: JRC/WOfS/EPI flood showed a bare '—' that could mean failure OR zero, and the nearby-DA radius was unstated. After: the reads get time to return a real value (0 for a dry lot); a genuine failure says 'Couldn't retrieve'; the radius reads '500 m'.

functions.name: _query_jrc_surface_water
functions.input: lat, lng for the JRC occurrence raster sample
functions.output: the water-occurrence percent (0 for a dry point) with the GDAL HTTP timeout raised to 30s inside a 60s outer guard
functions.if_none: returns null only on a failed/timed-out read, which the UI shows as 'Couldn't retrieve'

functions.name: _query_dea_wofs
functions.input: lat, lng for the DEA WOfS WCS GeoTIFF download
functions.output: the water-observed frequency percent with the WCS download timeout raised to 30s inside a 60s outer guard
functions.if_none: returns null only on a failed read, shown as 'Couldn't retrieve'

values: N/A - flood screening percentages and timeout constants, not regulatory values.
queries: N/A - no DB query; only the JRC vsicurl read and the WOfS/EPI HTTP timeouts changed.

break_it.scenario: JRC vsicurl read still exceeds 30s because the global tile is not cloud-optimized
break_it.what_happens: the read fails and the field shows 'Couldn't retrieve' instead of a value
break_it.repro: sample a point where GDAL must fetch large non-tiled strips
break_it.how: the outer 60s guard bounds it and the honest 'couldn't retrieve' message is shown, never a false 0; the authoritative EPI flood flag is still served from PostGIS in the Environmental card

break_it.scenario: A genuine zero-water reading is mistaken for a failure
break_it.what_happens: a real 0 could be hidden behind 'couldn't retrieve'
break_it.how: JRC/WOfS return 0.0 (not null) for a genuine zero, so 0 renders as '0' and only a true null (failed read) shows 'couldn't retrieve'

break_it.scenario: Raising the flood budget to 70s makes the brief longer and risks the stream cutoff again
break_it.how: the companion Trigger.dev maxDuration was raised 120->300s; flood sub-queries run concurrently so the section completes at ~max(sub-query) ~= 60s, under the 70s budget

post_merge.secrets: None - JRC (GCS) and DEA WOfS (WCS) are keyless public sources.
post_merge.other_repo: plotdetect-agents: trigger/intelligence-brief.ts maxDuration 120->300 must be deployed (npx trigger.dev deploy) for the brief tail to render.
post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run the Haberfield brief: JRC/WOfS show a real value (0% for this dry ridge) or an honest 'Couldn't retrieve'; the nearby-DA description reads '500 m'; after the maxDuration deploy, Terrain/Pre-DA/Confidence Summary render again.
